item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q020_syntaxin_fragment_reclassification","answer":"The fragment-based resemblance to spectrin should be interpreted as a local structural similarity, not an independent assignment of the complete syntaxin domain to a spectrin fold or evidence of spectrin ancestry. In SCOPe 2.08, 1br0 (d1br0a_) and all three classified chains of 1ez3 (d1ez3a_, d1ez3b_, d1ez3c_) share a.47.2.1 with 1dn1 chain B (d1dn1b_): the t-snare proteins family, within the t-snare proteins superfamily a.47.2, STAT-like fold a.47, and All alpha proteins class a. The annotations for d1br0a_ and d1ez3a_ explicitly describe three-helical fragments resembling one spectrin repeat and flag missing secondary structure amounting to less than one-third of the common domain. The STAT-like fold is described as a four-long-helix bundle.\n\nThus, the fuller structure supplies the architectural context needed to reinterpret the fragments. Their shared family and superfamily placement supports a homologous syntaxin relationship; the STAT-like fold designation alone does not establish homology to STAT proteins or justify transferring STAT signaling functions. Likewise, the spectrin-like fragment geometry does not justify transferring spectrin function. Fragment templates remain useful for the covered region, but should not define complete-domain topology, boundaries, or representative selection without checking coverage. Prefer a complete, validated structure for those purposes. Although 1dn1 B is the historical fuller-domain reference, 1dn1 was superseded by 3c98; SCOPe 2.08 annotates d1dn1b_ as an automated match to d3c98b_. This is a correction of interpretation as structural coverage improves, not evidence of a biological fold transition.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_pdb_entry","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains","mcp__scope__get_scop_node","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1br0/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1ez3/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1dn1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1br0a_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1br0a_/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1ez3a_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1ez3a_/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1dn1b_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1dn1b_/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47654/annotations"]}]}
